import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Fibonacci transform satisfying $|a(n)| = F(n+1)$

The sequence $a(n)$ satisfies the linear recurrence relation:
$$a(n) = 3a(n-1) - 4a(n-2) + 2a(n-3) - a(n-4)$$
with initial terms $a(0)=0, a(1)=1, a(2)=1, a(3)=0$.
The sequence takes values in $\mathbb{Z}$.

*References:*
- [A103311](https://oeis.org/A103311)
- [arxiv/2605.22763](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.22763) *Advancing Mathematics Research with AI-Driven Formal Proof Search* by George Tsoukalas et al.
-/

namespace OeisA103311


/--
The sequence $a(n)$ satisfies the linear recurrence relation:
$$a(n) = 3a(n-1) - 4a(n-2) + 2a(n-3) - a(n-4)$$
with initial terms $a(0)=0, a(1)=1, a(2)=1, a(3)=0$.
The sequence takes values in $\mathbb{Z}$.
-/
def a : ℕ → ℤ
| 0 => 0
| 1 => 1
| 2 => 1
| 3 => 0
| n + 4 => 3 * a (n + 3) - 4 * a (n + 2) + 2 * a (n + 1) - a n


@[category test, AMS 11]
lemma a_0 : a 0 = 0 := by rfl

@[category test, AMS 11]
lemma a_1 : a 1 = 1 := by rfl

@[category test, AMS 11]
lemma a_2 : a 2 = 1 := by rfl

@[category test, AMS 11]
lemma a_3 : a 3 = 0 := by rfl

@[category test, AMS 11]
lemma a_4 : a 4 = -2 := by rfl


/--
Fibonacci transform satisfying $|a(n)| = F(n+1)$.

Conjecture: all elements in absolute value are Fibonacci numbers.

A formal proof has been found with the methods described in
[arxiv/2605.22763](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.22763).
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using formal_conjectures at
"https://github.com/mo271/formal-conjectures/blob/a32396489dcb8f86c3549b93aa358ac6a10a3a1f/FormalConjectures/OEIS/103311.wip.lean#L218"]
theorem a_abs_eq_fib (n : ℕ) : ∃ m : ℕ, Int.natAbs (a n) = Nat.fib m := by
    sorry

end OeisA103311

findings.description: The first sentence of the theorem docstring (line 66), also repeated in the module heading (line 20), asserts |a(n)| = F(n+1). This is false: a(4) = -2, whereas F(5) = 5. The Lean theorem correctly asserts that each absolute value equals some Fibonacci number, with an index that may depend on n. Thus the error is confined to the documentation.
findings.source_evidence: OEIS A103311 says: “Conjecture: all elements in absolute value are Fibonacci numbers,” not that the index is n+1. Its title is “A transform of the Fibonacci numbers.” Read in the official data mirror at https://raw.githubusercontent.com/oeis/oeisdata/main/seq/A103/A103311.seq. The official b-file https://oeis.org/A103311/b103311.txt records a(4) = -2.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the formula |a(n)| = F(n+1) from both locations. Use “A transform of the Fibonacci numbers” as the module heading and retain the accurate Fibonacci-membership sentence in the theorem docstring. Leave the Lean statement unchanged.

reformulations.difference: Lean defines the sequence by a fourth-order recurrence rather than by the Chebyshev transform followed by the binomial involution used in OEIS's primary description.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: OEIS explicitly supplies the same recurrence and initial values. Moreover, the two specified Riordan transforms take the generating function -x/(1-x-x²) to x(1-x)²/(1-3x+4x²-2x³+x⁴). Comparing coefficients gives initial values 0,1,1,0 and precisely the Lean recurrence for indices at least 4. These initial values and recurrence uniquely determine the sequence.

sources_consulted: OEIS A103311, revision #21 dated 20 August 2026, read through its official data mirror: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/oeis/oeisdata/main/seq/A103/A103311.seq (the main OEIS entry returned a browser challenge).

George Tsoukalas et al., Advancing Mathematics Research with AI-Driven Formal Proof Search, arXiv:2605.22763v2; abstract at https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.22763 and LaTeX source at https://arxiv.org/e-print/2605.22763, particularly the OEIS results paragraph.

Tom Adamczewski, OEIS Open: How many conjectures can language models turn into theorems?, arXiv:2608.11941v2; https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.11941 and https://arxiv.org/e-print/2608.11941, Appendix A, A103311 row.

review.notes: All seven declarations were checked. The definition and five test lemmas agree with OEIS; the first 20 terms also passed a direct Lean comparison with the b-file. Lean verified the recurrence's reindexing, equivalence of natAbs-based membership with integer-absolute-value membership, and counterexamples to the documentation's fixed-index formula. OEIS records a proof dated May 25, 2026, consistent with research solved. To check the formal-proof claim without accessing formal-conjectures on GitHub, I compiled the OEIS-linked AlphaProof Nexus artifact after updating its obsolete import, proved its sequence equal to OeisA103311.a, and transported its theorem to the reviewed statement. The resulting theorem depends only on [propext, Quot.sound]. Experiments are in /workspace/review/; the reviewed file remains identical to the specified commit.
